_comentario: First Economics, Part 2 (winter, days 66-130): the English text of each day of Aprendo economía -- the day's story ('historia') and the text of its activity ('actividad', with its 'tipo') -- and the words of weeks 14-26 ('semanas'). Everything else is the one in content/q2.json, page by page: see cargar_traduccion in tools/gen_economia.py and notes/02-english.md.

semanas.definicion: To take one thing and leave another, when you cannot have both.
The money Spain had before the euro.
A measure of weight: fruit, meat and bread are bought by the kilo.
To make things that other people will use or buy, like bread or the roscón.
To treat things well, so that they last a long time.
The things we have and can use to make other things.
What everyone decides together, by talking, so that everyone is happy with it.
The money we plan to spend on something, before we spend it.
What you have to give to get something: money, time or work.
Work that is done for other people, without making anything: delivering letters, making people better, teaching.
To make something that is broken work again.
What we want to achieve, like the money we save to buy something.
Everything that people have not made: trees, animals, water, the sun.

dias.historia: In the nativity scene, the Three Kings move a hand's width closer to the stable every night. Dani wants to ask them for ten toys, but Mum explains that you cannot have everything: you have to choose.
In the morning, the Kings in the nativity scene are a hand's width closer to the stable. Lucía writes in her notebook: “Who is moving them?” Meanwhile, Dani crosses toys off his letter.

frases: With money, we can have everything we want.
If you choose one thing, you leave another.
Choosing means thinking about what you want most.
The most expensive thing is always the best.

dias.historia: In the toy shop, everything has its price. Lucía has €12 for Dani's present, and she looks at the prices before choosing.
Dani crosses out and crosses out until there are only three toys left on his letter. Now he has to choose one. “The one I like best, not the shiniest one,” he says.
The club solves the case: it is Dad who moves the Kings! He reads until midnight next to the nativity scene. And Dani, at last, has chosen the toy for his letter.

checklist: I know what choosing means.
I know that, if I choose one thing, I leave another.
I can look at the prices before buying.
actividad.prompt: Draw the toy you would choose, and the one you would leave.

dias.historia: On Christmas Eve, inside one of Grandma's old exercise books, Lucía finds a treasure map and a strange coin. “It is a peseta,” says Grandma. “I paid with pesetas when I was your age.”

frases: Before the euro, people in Spain paid with pesetas.
Grandma paid with euros when she was a girl.
Today in Spain we pay with euros.
Pesetas and euros are the same money.

dias.historia: Grandma remembers the prices from when she was a girl: comics, ice creams, marbles... Everything was paid for in pesetas, with big, heavy coins.

actividad.texto: As a girl, Grandma bought a comic for 3 pesetas and an ice cream for 2 pesetas. How much did she spend altogether?

dias.historia: Lucía compares the things from when Grandma was a girl with the things of today. Some have changed a lot, like money and telephones, and others hardly at all.

actividad.pregunta: Is it from when Grandma was a girl, or from today?

dias.historia: Grandma kept her pesetas in a biscuit tin. Lucía keeps her euros in her piggy bank: today she has a €20 note, a €10 note, a €5 note and two €2 coins.

actividad.pregunta: How much money does Lucía have in her piggy bank?

dias.historia: Grandma gives Lucía the map. “I drew it when I was your age, in the village,” she says. “In the summer we will look for the treasure together.”

checklist: I know what a peseta is.
I know what money we pay with today.
I know that prices long ago were different.

dias.historia: For New Year's Eve, Dad buys grapes: twelve for each person. At the greengrocer's, a kilo of grapes costs €4, and at the market, €3. Dad compares before he buys.

actividad.pregunta: A kilo of grapes costs €4 at the greengrocer's and €3 at the market. Where is it cheaper? How much do you save?

dias.historia: Dad buys 2 kilos of grapes at the market. At home, Mum washes them and counts them: there are enough grapes for everyone, with some left over.

actividad.texto: A kilo of grapes costs €3. Dad buys 2 kilos. How much does he pay?

dias.historia: After the bowls are ready, there are 14 grapes left over. Mum says that Lucía, Dani and Grandma can share them out equally.

actividad.pregunta: Share 14 grapes between Lucía, Dani and Grandma. How many does each one get? Are there any left over?

dias.historia: Three grapes are missing from Dani's bowl. Who has eaten them? While the club investigates, Mum buys tangerines for pudding, and looks for where they are cheaper.

actividad.pregunta: A kilo of tangerines costs €3 at the market and €2 at the greengrocer's. Where is it cheaper? How much do you save?

dias.historia: Case solved: Dani has a purple mouth and grape pips in his slipper. He ate three grapes to practise! At midnight, with the chimes of the clock, everyone eats theirs.

checklist: I know what a kilo is.
I can compare prices in two shops.
I know how much I save if I buy where it is cheaper.
actividad.prompt: Draw your family eating the twelve grapes.

dias.historia: On Three Kings' Day, the family buys a roscón at the baker's. The baker gets up at four o'clock to produce the roscones for the whole neighbourhood: he kneads them, bakes them and decorates them.

actividad.pregunta: Who produces each thing?

dias.historia: Lucía asks the baker how he makes the roscón. He laughs: “With flour, eggs, patience... and a hidden bean! Whoever finds it pays for the roscón next year.”

actividad.pregunta: How is the roscón made?
pasos: The flour is kneaded with the eggs.
The bean is hidden in the dough.
It is baked.
It is decorated with fruit and sugar.

dias.historia: For the Three Kings' tea, Mum buys the roscón and a churro for Dani. At the baker's, everything has its price on a label.

actividad.pregunta: Mum buys the roscón and a churro. How much does she pay?

dias.historia: At home, everyone puts on the paper crown from the roscón. Dad says that some people produce things and others buy them, and that sometimes we are both: Grandma knits scarves and buys bread.

actividad.pregunta: Producing or buying?

dias.historia: When they cut the roscón, the knife hits something hard in the slice with the cherry. It is the bean! Grandma has got it, and she laughs: next year, she will pay for the roscón.

checklist: I know what produce means.
I know who produces bread.
I know that some people produce and others buy.
actividad.prompt: Draw the roscón de Reyes, with its hidden bean.

dias.historia: Back at school, there is a snowman in the playground, with an old scarf that smells of coffee. Whoever made it looks after their things: the scarf is very old, but it is as good as new.

actividad.pregunta: Looking after things, or not?
cosas: keeps the pencils in their case
leaves the bike out in the rain
puts the lids on the felt tips
throws the school bag on the floor

dias.historia: The prints of some big boots go from the snowman to the caretaker's room. Boots like that, if they are looked after, last for years: they are cleaned, dried and put away.

actividad.pregunta: How do you look after each thing?
pares: under cover, out of the rain

dias.historia: Paco, the caretaker, gets to school at seven o'clock, before anyone else. His scarf has a hole in it, but he does not throw it away: he takes it to be mended.

actividad.texto: A new scarf costs €12, and mending the old one costs €3. How much does Paco save by mending it?

dias.historia: Hugo left his sledge outside all night, and it has broken. Now he is saving for another one: he already has €5, and every week he puts away €5 more. He will look after the new one better.

actividad.pregunta: Hugo has €5 in his piggy bank, and he saves €5 every week. The sledge costs €25. How many weeks will it take?

dias.historia: Case solved: the big boots, the scarf that smells of coffee and the time... Paco made the snowman, at seven o'clock! Paco laughs: “Look after it well, or it will melt.”

checklist: I know what looking after things means.
I know that looking after things is cheaper than buying new ones.
I can look after my toys and my books.
actividad.prompt: Draw something of yours that you look after very well.

dias.historia: Hugo wants a periscope to spy from behind the hedge, but he does not buy one: he makes it with the resources he has at home. A cardboard box, two small mirrors and some tape.

actividad.pregunta: Is it useful for making the periscope?

dias.historia: Hugo writes the instructions, so that the club can make periscopes too. But the steps have got mixed up, and now he does not know which one comes first.

actividad.pregunta: In what order do you make the periscope?
pasos: Make two holes in the box.
Stick the mirrors in at a slant.
Close the box with tape.
Look through the bottom hole.

dias.historia: From behind the hedge, with the periscope, the club can see the street without anyone seeing them: Pedro with his cat, the postwoman, a dog in a coat...

actividad.prompt: Draw Hugo's periscope, and what you can see from the hedge.

dias.historia: You can make lots of things with what you have at home. Sofía makes a kite with paper and canes, and Lucía makes a puppet with an old sock.

actividad.pregunta: What is each thing made with?

dias.historia: Hugo's periscope works so well that the club makes three more, one for each of them. They have spent almost nothing: just some tape and a bit of imagination.

checklist: I know what resources are.
I can make things with what there is at home.
I can follow instructions in order.
actividad.prompt: Draw something you would make with two cardboard tubes and some tape.

dias.historia: The club is arguing: everyone wants to be in charge. On Peace Day, Marta suggests that they talk until they reach an agreement. They decide to take turns in charge: one week each.

frases: To reach an agreement, you have to talk and listen.
In an agreement, the one who shouts loudest always wins.
Taking turns to be in charge is an agreement.
If there is an agreement, you have to keep it.
One person decides an agreement on their own.

dias.historia: In the morning, the sign on the club's hut has disappeared. Sofía thinks Hugo took it, and Hugo thinks Sofía did. Before anyone gets cross, Lucía suggests they investigate together.

actividad.pregunta: Is this how to reach an agreement?

dias.historia: While they investigate, the club counts its spare cards: they have 14. They reach an agreement: they share them out equally, and any left over stay in the club's box.

actividad.pregunta: Share 14 cards between Lucía, Sofía and Hugo. How many does each one get? Are there any left over?

dias.historia: The club finds clues: the tape on the sign was old, there was a gale last night, and Pedro's bin was in the middle of the street this morning. Who took the sign down?

actividad.pregunta: How do you reach an agreement?
pasos: Everyone says what they want.
Everyone listens to the others.
We look for something good for everyone.
We do what we have decided.

dias.historia: Case solved: the wind took the sign down! It was nobody's fault. The club makes a new sign, with strong tape, and keeps its agreement: today Sofía starts being in charge.

checklist: I know what an agreement is.
I can take turns to talk, and listen.
I can keep to what we all decide together.
actividad.prompt: Draw the club making the new sign, all together.

dias.historia: For Dad's birthday, Mum, Lucía and Dani are planning a treasure hunt. Before buying anything, they make a budget: they have €30 for the cake, the balloons and the present.

actividad.pregunta: The cake, the balloons and the present: how much does it all cost?

dias.historia: The present is a book about birds, because Dad loves watching them from the window. With the cake and the balloons, they have spent €28 of the €30 in the budget.

actividad.texto: They have €30 and they spend €28. How much do they have left?

dias.historia: Dani wants to add something to the party, paid for from his piggy bank. He cannot decide between a candle and a party hat: he does not have enough money for both.
Mum collects the cake from the cake shop. It costs €15, and she pays with a €20 note. The woman in the shop gives her the change, and Mum counts it before putting it away.
On Saturday, Dad follows the clues in code all round the house. At the end of the plan he finds his present, and says it is the best birthday ever: and without going over the budget!

checklist: I know what a budget is.
I can add up what I am going to spend.
I can work out what I have left.
actividad.prompt: Draw a birthday party, and what it would cost.

dias.historia: For Carnival, Lucía wants to dress up as a detective. The costume in the shop costs €20; if she makes it herself, the cost is €5 of fabric... and two afternoons of work.

actividad.texto: The costume in the shop costs €20, and making it at home costs €5. How much does Lucía save by making it herself?

dias.historia: Lucía and Grandma make the costume together: the raincoat, the hat and, of course, the magnifying glass. It takes them two afternoons, but they have a lovely time.

actividad.pregunta: How is the costume made?
pasos: The costume is drawn on paper.
The fabric is bought.
It is cut out and sewn.
It is worn for the first time in the parade.

dias.historia: In the parade, everyone wears a different costume: some bought, some homemade and some borrowed. They all cost something, even if it is not always money.

actividad.pregunta: What does each costume cost?
pares: you must give it back clean

dias.historia: After the parade, next to the steps of the stage, there is a purple and silver mask with a grown-up's elastic. Whose can it be? Nora, the new girl in the class, says it is very pretty.

actividad.pregunta: A mask costs €4 at the bargain shop and €7 at the fancy dress shop. Where is it cheaper? How much do you save?

dias.historia: Case solved: the mask belongs to Marta, the teacher, who dressed up for the parade. Nora has helped to find the clues, and the club invites her to its hut.

checklist: I know what the cost of something is.
I know that time is a cost too.
I can think about whether it is better to make it or buy it.
actividad.prompt: Draw the costume you would make yourself, and what you would need.

dias.historia: Martín writes Dani a letter from the village. The postwoman brings it: she does not make anything, but she provides a service for everyone, because she takes the letters from house to house.

actividad.pregunta: Making things or providing a service?

dias.historia: Dani answers Martín with a drawing of the snowman. To send the letter, you have to pay for the stamp at the post office.

actividad.pregunta: Sending the letter costs €3. Dani pays with a €5 note. How much change does he get?

dias.historia: In the letter, Martín says that the old mill in the village is going to be a museum. Lots of people will work there: some will show visitors round the mill, and others will sell the tickets.

actividad.pregunta: What service does each one provide?

dias.historia: Martín also says that the tortoise stone is not in the meadow any more: it has been moved to the mill garden. But the well does not move, so the map is still useful.

frases: The postwoman provides a service.
A service is always something you can touch.
The doctor provides a service when she makes us better.
To send a letter, you have to pay for the stamp.
Nobody provides services.

dias.historia: Dani and Lucía look at Grandma's map: “From the well, ten steps.” If the well is still in its place, so is the treasure. They cannot wait for the summer!

checklist: I know what a service is.
I know who brings the letters.
I can work out the change.
actividad.prompt: Draw someone who provides a service in your neighbourhood.

dias.historia: The plants in the classroom go droopy on Mondays. What is wrong with them? Marta says they must find out soon: if it is not fixed in time, they will have to buy new plants.

actividad.pregunta: Can it be fixed?
cosas: a chair with a wobbly leg

dias.historia: The club investigates: the plants have water, because Marta waters them on Fridays. And the geranium on Marta's desk looks lovely. What is different about the ones by the window?

actividad.pregunta: What do you need to fix it?

dias.historia: Hugo takes a close look at the window: the catch is broken, and the wind blows it open. At the weekend, with the heating off, the plants get cold!

actividad.pregunta: How do you fix it in time?
pasos: Someone sees that the catch is broken.
Paco is told.
Paco changes the catch.
The plants do not get cold any more.

dias.historia: Paco fixes the catch in no time. Marta works it out: if they had not fixed it, they would have had to buy new plants every week.

actividad.texto: Five new plants cost €20, and fixing the catch costs €4. How much does the class save?

dias.historia: The next Monday, the plants by the window are green and standing up straight. Marta thanks the club: fixing it in time cost much less than waiting.

checklist: I know what fixing means.
I know that fixing things in time costs less.
I know what you need to fix some things.
actividad.prompt: Draw something broken at your house, and how you would fix it.

dias.historia: The class goes to the planetarium. In the shop, Hugo sees a small telescope that costs €40. He sets himself a goal: he has €10, and he will save €5 every week until he can buy it.

actividad.pregunta: Hugo has €10 and he saves €5 every week. The telescope costs €40. How many weeks will it take?

dias.historia: At the planetarium, the guide talks about the planets: the hottest, the biggest, the one with rings... Hugo writes it all down, because he wants to make a wall display about a planet.

frases: A goal is something we want to achieve.
To reach a goal, sometimes you have to wait.
If you save a little every week, you never reach your goal.
A goal has to be very easy.

dias.historia: Every Sunday, Hugo opens his piggy bank and counts what he has saved: first the notes, then the coins. How much more does he need for his goal?

actividad.pregunta: How much money does Hugo have in his piggy bank?

dias.historia: Hugo's wall display is about a red planet, with two small moons. Which one can it be? Meanwhile, in the planetarium shop, a man buys a telescope with a €50 note.
Case solved: Hugo's planet is Mars, red and with two moons. And his goal is still there: every week, €5 more in the piggy bank, until he has enough for the telescope.

checklist: I know what a goal is.
I can save a little every week.
I can count the money in my piggy bank.
actividad.prompt: Draw your goal: something you would save up for.

dias.historia: Little bits of wool are disappearing from Grandma's basket. Who is taking them? While the club investigates, Grandma says that nature gives us lots of things: wool, wood, water...

actividad.pregunta: Does nature give it to us?

dias.historia: Lucía finds a brown feather next to the basket, and Hugo sees a red thread high up in the ivy in the garden. Who can climb so high?

actividad.pregunta: Where does it come from?

dias.historia: Grandma gives Lucía €20 for helping her in the garden all week. Lucía thinks about her three jars: save, spend and share.

actividad.pregunta: Lucía has €20. She puts €6 in the spend jar and €4 in the share jar. How much does she put in the save jar?

dias.historia: From the window, the club sees a blackbird singing on the wall. Another one flies into the ivy with something red in its beak... It is a bit of Grandma's wool!

actividad.prompt: Draw the blackbirds' nest in the ivy, with Grandma's wool.

dias.historia: Case solved: the blackbirds are making their nest with Grandma's wool. She leaves more for them in the basket. “It is my present to nature,” she says.

checklist: I know what nature is.
I know what things nature gives us.
I know that we must look after it.
actividad.prompt: Draw what you like most about nature.
